items.question:
A clinical trials director at an academic medical centre ran an eight-week Claude pilot for protocol synopsis drafting across five trials. Time-per-synopsis dropped by 40%. When presenting to the grants committee, a member objects: 'We cannot verify that any of those time savings were real, because no one tracked what the freed time was used for.'

What does the committee member's objection reveal about the ROI measurement approach?

options.A: The pilot was too short to establish a meaningful baseline; eight weeks is insufficient for clinical trials work.
options.B: The committee member is applying an unusually rigorous standard; time-per-task reduction is a widely accepted proxy for productivity improvement.
options.C: The measurement captured an efficiency metric but did not verify how the freed time was redeployed, leaving open whether the gain produced any realised value or was simply absorbed invisibly.
options.D: The team should have tracked protocol submission quality scores in addition to time, as quality improvement is a more credible metric for a scientific committee.

items.question:
A federal agency's AI programme lead is rolling out Claude to 80 policy analysts across six directorates for drafting policy briefs and regulatory comment responses. She wants to ensure standardised output quality while preserving directorate-specific regulatory expertise in the prompting process.

Which TWO approaches best achieve both goals simultaneously? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Establish a central prompt library with approved templates for each brief type, maintained by the AI programme office and versioned with a change log.
options.B: Assign each directorate a designated prompt steward who customises the central templates for directorate-specific regulatory terminology and context, and is accountable for template quality.
options.C: Require all 80 analysts to complete identical prompt-engineering certification before tool access, ensuring a uniform skill baseline across all directorates.
options.D: Allow each directorate to develop its own independent prompt library without central coordination, preserving complete autonomy over template design.
options.E: Conduct monthly cross-directorate prompt review sessions where analysts share output samples and the programme office arbitrates quality disputes.

items.question:
A programme associate at a youth services non-profit has been assigned to write volunteer recruitment emails using Claude. The executive director previously wrote these emails by hand in a warm, community-focused voice. The associate wants to match the director's tone without guessing. The director has one hour to help.

What is the SIMPLEST way the director can ensure consistent voice from the first session?

options.A: Send the associate links to Anthropic's public documentation so she can self-study Claude's text generation capabilities.
options.B: Ask IT to configure a shared Claude Project with the director's preferred tone described in the custom instructions field.
options.C: Schedule a live session where the director explains the organisation's tone philosophy and core messaging principles.
options.D: Provide two or three past successful campaign emails as examples alongside a brief prompt template describing the target audience, tone, and required message structure.

items.question:
A customer experience director at a mobile telecoms company deployed Claude to a 50-person CX strategy team six months ago for competitive analysis summaries and customer-insight briefs. Usage data shows 12 analysts are heavy users; 38 have used the tool fewer than five times total. When the director asks the 12 heavy users why adoption stalled, they say: 'We don't know — we think people just don't have time to figure it out.'

What should the director investigate FIRST to diagnose the actual root cause?

options.A: Whether the 38 low-use analysts have heavier BAU workloads that prevent them investing time in learning a new tool.
options.B: Whether the tool's login process or interface creates enough friction that analysts abandon it before completing a first useful session.
options.C: Whether the enablement programme connected Claude's capabilities to the analysts' specific recurring tasks, or demonstrated generic capabilities without task-level relevance.
options.D: Whether the 12 heavy users are in a sub-team with more analytical tasks, making AI genuinely less applicable to the 38 others' roles.

items.question:
A chief risk officer at a regional bank introduced a Claude-assisted workflow twelve months ago for drafting regulatory correspondence. The projected benefit was a 30% drafting time reduction. After twelve months, the actual reduction is 8%, compliance officers spend significant time correcting Claude's interpretation of regulatory guidance, and two compliance officers have independently reported that AI-drafted letters occasionally mischaracterise the bank's risk position.

Which decision is MOST defensible given this evidence?

options.A: Continue and invest in a more intensive prompt-engineering training programme to close the remaining performance gap over the next quarter.
options.B: Formally sunset the workflow, conduct a structured post-mortem, and halt AI-assisted regulatory correspondence drafting while evaluating alternatives.
options.C: Narrow the workflow scope to the lowest-sensitivity correspondence types, retaining AI assistance only where regulatory mischaracterisation risk is lowest.
options.D: Commission a technical audit of the prompts used to determine whether improved prompt engineering could close the performance gap before taking structural action.

items.question:
An e-commerce merchandising manager at a grocery retailer wants to start a Claude pilot. He is choosing between using Claude to draft product description copy for new SKU launches, or using Claude to recommend dynamic pricing adjustments based on competitor data he manually inputs. Both would save time if they work.

Which is the BETTER first pilot use case?

options.A: Product description copy, because errors in copy are low-stakes and easily corrected before publication, providing a safe environment to learn and iterate.
options.B: Dynamic pricing, because structured numerical inputs make output easier to verify objectively against the source data.
options.C: Dynamic pricing, because demonstrating revenue impact will make the ROI case more compelling than copy productivity.
options.D: Both simultaneously so the manager can benchmark which produces higher productivity gain in the same time window.

items.question:
A lean operations director at an auto-parts manufacturer has documented a Claude workflow for drafting 8D problem-solving reports — covering the prompt templates and step sequence. In a dry-run session, three supervisors attempted the workflow with the runbook and produced structurally correct outputs but lacking the specific causal language that meets the plant's quality standard. The director is preparing to roll out to 15 supervisors next week.

What should the director do NEXT?

options.A: Postpone the rollout until all 15 supervisors complete a refresher course on 8D methodology to ensure their domain knowledge is sufficient.
options.B: Proceed with the rollout as planned and address individual quality gaps through supervisor performance reviews after the first month.
options.C: Add annotated examples of well-written causal sections to the runbook alongside the existing templates, so supervisors have a concrete quality reference before rollout.
options.D: Switch to a more capable model tier that produces more precise causal language by default, removing the dependency on supervisor prompting skill.

items.question:
A post-production head at a film studio is proposing a Claude-assisted workflow for drafting VFX shot breakdown reports — currently a manual process taking two hours per feature. She needs to select success metrics for a six-month pilot that will be evaluated by the studio's production operations committee.

Which TWO metrics would give the committee the clearest evidence that the workflow is delivering value? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Number of VFX supervisors who complete Claude onboarding within the first four weeks of the pilot.
options.B: Average time to produce a complete VFX shot breakdown report, measured before and after workflow adoption.
options.C: Employee satisfaction score for the VFX supervision team, collected at the midpoint of the pilot.
options.D: Percentage of AI-drafted shot breakdown reports accepted by the production team without substantive revision on first review.
options.E: Total number of Claude sessions initiated by VFX supervisors per week across the pilot period.

items.question:
A project director at an offshore wind developer is introducing a Claude workflow for drafting environmental impact assessment sections to a team of 12 environmental consultants. The firm's senior partner, who is not using Claude himself, has publicly expressed scepticism that AI can 'understand the nuance of offshore environmental regulations.' Two junior consultants have mentioned his scepticism as a reason they have not tried the tool.

What is the MOST effective way to address this specific adoption barrier?

options.A: Engage the senior partner directly: share specific examples of Claude-assisted EIA sections reviewed and approved by the firm's most experienced environmental scientists, then invite him to observe a live session.
options.B: Bypass the senior partner's influence by framing the tool adoption as a firm-wide directive from the managing director rather than a team decision.
options.C: Wait for the senior partner to retire or move to a different project before accelerating tool adoption across the team.
options.D: Brief the junior consultants privately that the senior partner's concerns are technically unfounded, and encourage them to use the tool independently.

items.question:
An instructional design lead at an online university has a team of four course designers who use Claude to draft learning objectives and module descriptions for new course shells. The team lead reviews all outputs before they go to faculty, and she keeps having to rewrite the same structural problems — learning objectives that are not written in the Bloom's Taxonomy action-verb format required by the university's QA framework.

What is the MOST direct fix for this recurring structural problem?

options.A: Require each course designer to complete a training module on Bloom's Taxonomy before their next Claude session.
options.B: Have the team lead add the Bloom's Taxonomy correction step to her review checklist so she catches all violations systematically.
options.C: Update the shared prompt template for learning objectives to specify the Bloom's Taxonomy action-verb requirement explicitly and include two examples of compliant objectives.
options.D: Switch to a more capable model tier that has stronger instructional design knowledge and will apply Bloom's Taxonomy automatically.

items.question:
An underwriting operations manager at a commercial insurer has built a Claude workflow for drafting declination letters. The workflow is effective when she uses it, but when her two underwriting assistants follow the same runbook, they occasionally submit letters that incorrectly apply the policy exclusion language — a problem that never arose with the manager's own use. The runbook covers the prompts and step sequence.

What is the MOST likely gap in the runbook that explains the discrepancy?

options.A: The runbook was not approved by the legal department before being distributed to the assistants, creating a governance gap in the documentation chain.
options.B: The assistants are applying the prompts correctly, but Claude produces lower-quality legal language for users without underwriting titles in their session context.
options.C: The assistants are accessing a different model tier than the manager, producing less precise exclusion language under identical prompts.
options.D: The runbook does not include the manager's decision rules for selecting the correct exclusion clause given the specific risk type, leaving assistants to infer a critical selection step that the manager performs automatically from experience.

items.question:
A CMO at a biotech company presents an AI programme review to the board. Her team used Claude over nine months for drafting scientific abstracts, conference biopharma briefings, and investor relations materials. She presents data showing a 35% reduction in drafting time and a 90% user satisfaction rate. The board chair asks: 'What did that time reduction translate to in terms of outputs, team capacity, or revenue impact?' The CMO cannot answer.

What does the board chair's question reveal about the programme's ROI measurement?

options.A: The CMO should have presented the data differently — expressing the time reduction in dollar terms using average fully-loaded salary costs to make the financial impact self-evident.
options.B: The programme measured inputs and sentiment but did not track what the organisation received in exchange for the freed capacity — no output, throughput, or strategic impact measure was collected.
options.C: The board chair is applying unreasonable standards by expecting an AI programme to demonstrate revenue impact when scientific communications work does not directly generate revenue.
options.D: A nine-month window is insufficient to demonstrate revenue impact for a biotech company; the programme should have been measured over at least two fiscal years.

items.question:
A route planning lead at an air freight operator has successfully deployed a Claude workflow for drafting delay-notification emails to cargo clients. Three of his six team members use it consistently and report saving 45 minutes per shift. The other three never adopted it and draft notifications manually. All six received the same initial training two months ago.

What is the MOST actionable next step to convert the three non-adopters?

options.A: Schedule a thirty-minute session where the three active users walk through their specific prompts and workflow with the three non-adopters, using a real delay scenario from the previous week.
options.B: Issue a team-level mandate requiring all six team members to use Claude for every delay notification going forward.
options.C: Remove the non-adopters from the delay-notification task and reassign it to the three active users to maintain consistent quality.
options.D: Upgrade the tool to include a feature that automatically drafts notifications from the flight management system, removing the prompting step entirely.

items.question:
A knowledge management director at a large management consultancy has built a library of Claude prompt templates for common deliverable types: client situation summaries, opportunity assessments, and capability profiles. Consultants use them regularly. After six months, several teams report that the templates for capability profiles are producing outdated service descriptions because the firm added three new practice areas not reflected in the templates.

What governance practice would MOST directly prevent this type of content staleness?

options.A: Require consultants to submit a formal IT change request each time they believe a template needs updating so all changes are centrally logged before implementation.
options.B: Train all consultants to monitor firm capability announcements themselves and update their individual working copies of the template when they notice changes.
options.C: Accept that prompt templates will periodically become outdated and instruct consultants to supplement the template with current capability information in their individual prompts.
options.D: Assign a named owner to each template who is added to the firm's capabilities-update distribution list and is accountable for updating affected templates within a defined time window whenever relevant capabilities change.

items.question:
A digital transformation director at a state tax authority is designing a Claude pilot for 15 tax analysts who process complex correspondence with business taxpayers. Responses to taxpayers must cite accurate code sections and never misrepresent taxpayer obligations. The director wants to run the most informative pilot possible within a three-month window.

Which TWO design choices would MOST effectively balance learning velocity with the accuracy risks of this regulated context? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Limit the pilot scope to drafting internal analysis memos — not outbound taxpayer correspondence — so errors have no direct regulatory consequence during the learning period.
options.B: Run all 15 analysts simultaneously from day one to maximise the volume of pilot data within the three-month window.
options.C: Require every AI-assisted draft to be reviewed and approved by a senior analyst with the authority to correct citation errors before any output leaves the office.
options.D: Use a shadow mode during the first month: analysts draft responses manually as normal, Claude drafts in parallel, and quality is compared without using Claude's output externally.
options.E: Adopt Claude for all correspondence types immediately to generate the broadest possible learning dataset within the pilot window.

items.question:
A global sourcing manager at a fast-fashion retailer has rolled out a Claude workflow for drafting supplier risk assessment summaries. Three months in, she presents to the supply chain leadership team. She has data showing high user satisfaction and 100% adoption across her eight-person team. The supply chain director asks: 'But are the summaries actually better than what we had before?'

What does the director's question reveal about what was missing from the metrics presented?

options.A: The manager should have benchmarked her team's satisfaction against the industry average to contextualise the 100% satisfaction result.
options.B: Adoption and satisfaction are leading indicators of programme engagement but do not measure whether the quality of supplier risk summaries improved — no output-quality or decision-quality metric was collected.
options.C: The director is applying an unfair standard by expecting a quality improvement in a three-month window when behaviour change typically takes six months to manifest in output quality.
options.D: The manager should have measured the time taken per summary before and after, since speed improvement is the primary value proposition of AI tools.

items.question:
A client-solutions head at a global private bank is introducing Claude to 20 senior relationship managers who will use it to draft wealth management commentary for quarterly client review packs. The relationship managers are expert communicators with strong domain knowledge but low tolerance for generic outputs. Early testing produced technically correct but noticeably templated commentary that senior managers found embarrassing to send.

What enablement approach would MOST effectively address this gap before full rollout?

options.A: Deploy a locked prompt interface with pre-approved commentary templates so all managers produce consistent, bank-approved output.
options.B: Require managers to complete a twenty-hour prompt-engineering course so they can write sophisticated instructions that elicit personalised output.
options.C: Run a workshop where managers practise adding personalising context — client name, relationship history, specific portfolio events, manager's own framing — to an approved base template, and compare outputs.
options.D: Switch to a more capable model tier that produces less templated language and better understands private banking communication standards by default.

items.question:
A chief nursing officer at a large hospital system wants to scale a Claude-assisted shift-summary workflow from a four-nurse pilot unit to all 22 medical-surgical units — approximately 400 nursing staff. The pilot showed 28% time savings on shift summaries and strong quality acceptance by charge nurses. The CNO plans to roll out all 22 units simultaneously next month.

What is the MOST significant risk of the simultaneous all-units rollout strategy?

options.A: Nursing staff on all 22 units will generate more concurrent Claude usage than the hospital's IT infrastructure can reliably support.
options.B: The 28% time savings observed in the pilot unit may not replicate on units with heavier patient loads, making the ROI case difficult to sustain after rollout.
options.C: Charge nurses on the 21 non-pilot units will resist the workflow because they were not involved in developing it and may feel it was imposed without their input.
options.D: Any quality problem or adoption failure that emerges in one unit will be occurring simultaneously across all 22 units before it can be identified and corrected, multiplying harm and rework before the cause is understood.

items.question:
A continuous improvement lead at a steel manufacturer is introducing Claude to five process engineers for drafting non-conformance reports (NCRs). Each engineer currently writes NCRs differently, and the quality assurance manager reports spending an average of 20 minutes per NCR reformatting them to meet ISO documentation requirements. The CI lead wants to eliminate this reformatting burden.

What is the MOST direct solution?

options.A: Create a Claude prompt template for NCRs that specifies the ISO-required sections, mandatory fields, and documentation language standards, and distribute it to all five engineers.
options.B: Ask the QA manager to document the correct NCR format and send it to each engineer as a reference document they can consult while writing prompts.
options.C: Have the CI lead review all Claude-generated NCRs before they reach the QA manager, adding a second review step in the process.
options.D: Subscribe the team to a quality management system that enforces NCR formatting automatically without requiring Claude prompt customisation.

items.question:
A digital change lead at a large telecoms conglomerate is planning the organisation-wide rollout of Claude to 3,000 employees across customer-facing, technical, and corporate functions. Based on a six-month pilot across 200 employees, she has identified three critical success factors for the full deployment.

Which THREE elements are most essential to include in the full rollout plan? (Choose THREE)

options.A: A communications programme that explains the purpose of the rollout, addresses common concerns about AI, and sets clear expectations about how the tool will and will not be used.
options.B: Role-specific use-case guides showing employees in each function which tasks Claude is well-suited for and what the expected workflow looks like.
options.C: A standardised baseline measurement of key task metrics taken before rollout so improvements can be quantified against a credible pre-AI baseline.
options.D: A requirement that every employee complete a minimum of ten Claude sessions in the first two weeks to establish early usage habits.
options.E: An escalation and support pathway so employees who encounter unexpected outputs or concerns can get help without waiting for the next scheduled training cycle.

items.question:
A VP of quality at a contract research organisation manages 35 clinical research associates across eight study sites who draft protocol deviation summaries. Quality audits reveal significant variation in summary completeness and regulatory language across sites — some sites are consistently compliant while others require extensive rework. The VP wants to standardise quality without centralising all drafting work.

What approach would MOST effectively raise the floor across all sites?

options.A: Require all 35 CRAs to submit drafts to the VP's team for review before filing, centralising quality control without removing site-level authorship.
options.B: Deploy a shared Claude prompt template for protocol deviation summaries that encodes the required regulatory language, mandatory fields, and completeness criteria across all sites.
options.C: Conduct targeted training at the four under-performing sites to improve their understanding of protocol deviation documentation requirements.
options.D: Transfer the highest-performing CRAs from compliant sites to under-performing sites to model correct practice.

items.question:
A grants coordinator at a small rural community foundation writes grant reports to twelve different funders. Each funder has different report formatting requirements, and the coordinator currently spends 30 minutes per report manually reformatting content she has already written for the foundation's internal records.

How should she use Claude prompt templates to MOST directly address this reformatting burden?

options.A: Create a single universal Claude prompt that generates one master report covering all twelve funders' requirements simultaneously.
options.B: Ask Claude to memorise all twelve funders' requirements across multiple sessions so the coordinator does not need to specify them each time.
options.C: Build a separate prompt template for each funder that specifies that funder's required sections, field labels, word limits, and formatting conventions, and reuse it for every reporting cycle.
options.D: Use Claude to reformat the internal record into each funder's format interactively in each session, without a saved template, to maintain flexibility.

items.question:
An editorial director at a trade publication introduced a Claude workflow six months ago for generating first drafts of sponsored content articles. Initially, the workflow delivered faster drafts. Over the past three months, advertisers have begun requesting more rewrites than before, the editorial team's relationship with two advertisers has deteriorated over content disputes, and three of the five editors now route around the workflow and draft manually. Usage has dropped to 22% of sponsored content.

Which action is MOST appropriate at this stage?

options.A: Provide additional prompt-engineering training to the two editors still using the workflow so they can improve output quality and model the approach for the others.
options.B: Mandate workflow use for all sponsored content editors to restore adoption levels and gather enough usage data to improve the prompts.
options.C: Commission a reader survey to determine whether readers perceive any quality difference between AI-assisted and manually drafted sponsored content.
options.D: Suspend the workflow for sponsored content, conduct a review with the editors and affected advertisers, and assess whether a redesigned workflow can address the root causes.

items.question:
A provost's office at a large public research university is one year into a Claude rollout across academic administration — budget analysts, programme coordinators, and academic affairs staff. The provost wants evidence that the programme has improved the administration's efficiency and output quality before approving a second-year budget. No metrics were collected before rollout.

Which TWO approaches would MOST credibly reconstruct a value case despite the missing baseline? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Ask staff to retrospectively estimate how long the same tasks took before Claude and compare to current measured times, acknowledging the inherent limitation of self-reported recall.
options.B: Compare the current year's output volume and cycle times (e.g., budget reports produced, days-to-complete policy briefs) against the same metrics from the prior year's administrative records.
options.C: Present user satisfaction scores as the primary ROI evidence, arguing that high satisfaction is a reliable proxy for productivity improvement.
options.D: Commission an external benchmarking study comparing the university's administration metrics to a national higher-education benchmark to infer pre-rollout performance.
options.E: Review existing administrative records from the year before rollout (e.g., budget cycle completion dates, report production logs) to reconstruct a proxy baseline.

items.question:
A last-mile delivery startup's operations lead deployed Claude four months ago for a team of 12 operations coordinators who draft exception-handling notes for failed delivery attempts. Adoption started strong at 90% but has dropped to 55% as the team has grown from 12 to 24 coordinators. Exit interviews with non-adopters find no technical complaints — new hires say they 'just started doing it the way everyone else showed them' without using Claude.

What is the PRIMARY adoption barrier to investigate?

options.A: The original 12 coordinators have developed such advanced prompting skills that new hires feel intimidated by the expertise gap and avoid the tool to escape unfavourable comparison.
options.B: Claude's output style is not calibrated for the startup's specific exception-handling language, creating a quality gap that discourages new hires from continuing after a poor first attempt.
options.C: The Claude workflow was not included in the formal onboarding documentation for new hires, so they learned exception-handling from peer observation of the manual approach and were never introduced to the AI workflow as the team standard.
options.D: The startup's rapid headcount growth has created workload pressure that prevents new hires from investing time in learning any unfamiliar tool, including Claude.

items.question:
A VP of claims at a P&C insurer wants to scale a Claude-assisted claims-summary workflow from a 15-person complex-loss team to all 200 claims examiners across three lines of business: property, auto, and liability. The complex-loss pilot used a single highly refined prompt developed over six months. The VP plans to deploy the same prompt to all 200 examiners.

What is the MOST significant flaw in this scaling plan?

options.A: Deploying to 200 examiners at once without a phased rollout exceeds the recommended change management ceiling for a single AI deployment event.
options.B: Six months of prompt development is insufficient validation time to deploy a prompt into a regulated production claims environment.
options.C: The 200 examiners will each develop personal prompt modifications that fragment the standardisation the VP is trying to achieve.
options.D: A prompt developed and refined for complex-loss claims will produce structurally inappropriate summaries for property, auto, and liability claims, which have different terminology, evidence types, coverage frameworks, and documentation requirements.

items.question:
An operations COO at an investment management firm has run a four-week Phase 1 Claude pilot. Five operations analysts used Claude to draft trade-break resolution notes. Quality was good, prompt iteration has stabilised, and the analysts report 40% time savings per note. The COO is deciding whether to expand to Phase 2. She has two options: expand to 20 more analysts on the same trade-break task, or keep the same five analysts but add three new task types (cash reconciliation notes, position discrepancy summaries, and settlement failure reports).

What should the COO do NEXT before deciding between the two expansion options?

options.A: Launch both expansion tracks simultaneously to maximise learning and cover the most ground within the quarterly budget cycle.
options.B: Select one expansion track — either more users on the same task, or same users on new task types — and document in advance the specific quality criteria and timeline that will determine whether Phase 2 is successful.
options.C: Commission an independent technology review of the pilot results before committing to any Phase 2 expansion, to ensure the quality data is externally validated.
options.D: Extend Phase 1 for another four weeks with the same five analysts on the same task to accumulate more data before any expansion decision.

items.question:
A loss-prevention lead at a large grocery chain has developed a Claude workflow for writing shortage-investigation summary reports. The approach is effective and the reports consistently satisfy internal audit review. The lead is going on extended leave and wants the workflow handed to a colleague who has never used Claude. The lead has two hours before leaving.

Which documentation artefact would MOST effectively enable the colleague to produce audit-quality reports from day one?

options.A: A written runbook with the exact prompts used, the step-by-step sequence, what to do when Claude's first output needs adjustment, and two annotated examples of completed audit-quality reports.
options.B: An email introduction to the internal audit team explaining that a new person will be running the workflow and asking them to be patient during a transition period.
options.C: A summary of the principles behind effective prompting so the colleague can develop her own approach from first principles.
options.D: A shared Claude Project containing the loss-prevention policies the lead uploaded to inform Claude's responses during her sessions.

items.question:
A communications director at a renewable energy developer is rolling out Claude to eight communications staff for drafting stakeholder updates on construction projects. After four weeks of use, she notices that different staff members produce updates at very different quality levels — some are polished and technically accurate, while others are vague and miss key project milestones. The staff received the same one-hour orientation session.

What is the MOST likely cause of the quality variance and how should the director address it?

options.A: Some staff are more naturally talented communicators; the director should identify the best performers and have others route updates through them for editing.
options.B: The orientation session was too short to develop proficiency; the director should require all staff to complete a full-day Claude training programme.
options.C: The staff lack a shared quality reference — example updates and a prompt template specifying required milestones and technical accuracy checks — so each person is interpreting the quality standard differently.
options.D: The construction project details are too technically complex for Claude to handle accurately without being fine-tuned on the developer's engineering specifications.

items.question:
A care coordination head at a children's hospital is introducing a Claude workflow to 18 care coordinators for drafting patient-transition summaries when patients move from inpatient to outpatient care. Clinical accuracy and family-accessible language are both required. She needs to build the shared prompt template for this task.

Which TWO elements are MOST critical to include in the template to ensure outputs meet both requirements? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A requirement that the output begins with a one-paragraph administrative summary suitable for the discharging physician's review.
options.B: An explicit instruction to present all medical diagnoses and medication names in plain language accessible to a non-medical family, with clinical terms included parenthetically where required for record accuracy.
options.C: A character-count limit on the summary to ensure it fits within the hospital's electronic health record field constraints.
options.D: A required section structure listing the specific clinical accuracy elements that must be present: diagnosis, discharge medications, follow-up appointments, red-flag symptoms, and emergency contact instructions.
options.E: An instruction to generate the summary in a Q&A format matching the way families typically ask questions at discharge.

items.question:
A regulatory operations lead at a vaccine manufacturer is rolling out a Claude-assisted workflow for drafting adverse event narrative summaries to a team of 14 pharmacovigilance specialists. Three weeks in, adoption is 50%. The specialists who are not using the tool have not raised any stated objections — they simply have not engaged. The lead suspects they view the workflow as 'just another initiative' and are waiting to see if it disappears.

What approach would MOST effectively convert this passive non-adoption?

options.A: Run a structured peer-demonstration session where two or three adopting specialists walk through specific adverse event narrative scenarios, showing exactly how the workflow changes their approach and how much time each step saves — making the value concrete from colleagues doing the same work.
options.B: Issue a department head communication linking Claude workflow adoption to the team's annual performance objectives to create formal accountability.
options.C: Wait sixty more days before taking any action — passive non-adoption in pharmacovigilance teams often resolves organically as workflows prove their value through peer observation over time.
options.D: Schedule individual coaching sessions with each of the seven non-adopters to understand their personal concerns and address them one by one.

items.question:
A deputy commissioner at a regional transportation authority is presenting the ROI case for a twelve-month Claude programme to the authority's board. The programme saved an estimated 2,400 staff-hours of drafting work across planning documents and public consultation responses. The board approves the cost of the programme but asks the deputy commissioner: 'What did those 2,400 hours get redirected to?' The deputy commissioner cannot answer.

What does this question expose about the programme's design?

options.A: The programme failed to save enough hours to satisfy public sector board scrutiny; 2,400 staff-hours across twelve months is below the threshold that typically justifies an AI investment at authority level.
options.B: Public sector boards typically apply private-sector return-on-investment frameworks that are inappropriate for a government agency's value-creation context.
options.C: The board is primarily interested in citizen service delivery improvements, and the deputy commissioner should have led with service outcome data rather than efficiency data.
options.D: The programme was approved and run without a redeployment plan specifying what the freed staff hours would be used for, leaving the efficiency gain as unrealised capacity rather than converted value.

items.question:
A quality manager at a metal fabrication shop with 45 employees is considering a Claude pilot. She has identified two options: using Claude to draft customer quotation cover letters, or using Claude to draft corrective action plans for non-conformances. She wants to run the safer first pilot given her limited time to manage it.

Which use case is the BETTER first pilot, and why?

options.A: Corrective action plans, because they are reviewed by the quality team before implementation, ensuring any Claude errors are caught before manufacturing changes are triggered.
options.B: Corrective action plans, because the structured root-cause and containment format makes them more straightforward for Claude to generate than unstructured cover letters.
options.C: Customer quotation cover letters, because a drafting error in a cover letter can be identified and corrected before it causes any operational harm, whereas an incorrect corrective action plan may trigger physical manufacturing changes before the error is discovered.
options.D: Both simultaneously in a two-track pilot, so the quality manager can compare output quality across document types and choose the better use case based on evidence.

items.question:
A director of professional development at a boutique law firm has introduced Claude to 25 associates for drafting legal memoranda research summaries. After eight weeks, usage data shows that 18 associates use Claude regularly, while seven do not. The seven non-users are concentrated in two practice groups: employment law and IP litigation. When asked, they say 'our clients expect our personal expertise, not AI output.'

What is the MOST effective approach to address this specific resistance?

options.A: Require all 25 associates to demonstrate Claude usage in their time-billing records so non-adoption becomes visible to practice group leaders.
options.B: Reframe the tool explicitly as a research-acceleration assistant: Claude drafts the initial research sweep that the associate then refines, applies client-specific judgement to, and signs off on — preserving and demonstrating the associate's expertise.
options.C: Exclude the two practice groups from the programme since their client expectations may genuinely make AI-assisted work inappropriate for their work type.
options.D: Commission a client survey to determine whether employment law and IP litigation clients have any actual objection to AI-assisted research summaries.

items.question:
A network operations VP at a satellite operator is standardising a Claude-assisted workflow for drafting customer-impact notifications during network incidents. Notifications must be technically precise for enterprise customers while also being understood by non-technical customer contacts. The VP oversees eight network operations engineers and four customer success managers who jointly own customer communications.

Which TWO governance elements would MOST effectively ensure notification quality across all twelve staff? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A shared prompt template with two distinct output sections: a technical-details block for enterprise customer engineers, and a business-impact summary block for non-technical contacts — both generated in a single Claude session.
options.B: A post-incident review process where one engineer and one customer success manager jointly score each notification against defined quality criteria within 24 hours of incident resolution, to improve future drafts.
options.C: A two-person pre-release review gate in which the network engineer who drafted the notification verifies technical precision before sign-off, and the on-call customer success manager verifies the business-impact section for clarity and accessibility before the notification is sent.
options.D: A prompt template that includes example sentences demonstrating technically precise language alongside plain-language equivalents for the five most common incident types, as reference examples for staff.
options.E: A locked Claude interface that engineers and customer success managers access separately, with different system prompts pre-loaded for their respective audience contexts.

items.question:
A wealth management lead at a retail bank has a shared Claude prompt template used by 18 relationship bankers for drafting client portfolio commentary. The template has been in use for five months. Three months ago, the bank updated its suitability framework, but the template was not updated. Two bankers recently submitted commentary referencing the old suitability criteria, which the compliance team caught before client distribution.

What governance practice would MOST directly prevent this type of template lag?

options.A: Conduct a monthly team meeting where bankers review their prompt templates and self-report any outdated content they have noticed.
options.B: Require compliance team sign-off on all Claude-generated commentary before it reaches clients, regardless of how current the template is.
options.C: Train all 18 bankers to monitor regulatory and policy changes themselves and update their individual copies of the template independently.
options.D: Assign a named template owner who is notified when the suitability framework or any referenced policy changes, and who is accountable for updating the template within a defined time window before the change takes effect.

items.question:
An operations VP at a fast-casual restaurant chain has rolled out Claude to 15 district managers for drafting weekly operational compliance summaries. She wants to track whether the rollout is delivering value and report to the CEO in ninety days.

Which metric would give the CEO the CLEAREST early signal that the workflow is working as intended?

options.A: Reduction in average time per district manager to produce a completed compliance summary, compared to the baseline measured before rollout.
options.B: Number of Claude sessions initiated across all 15 district managers in the ninety-day window.
options.C: Percentage of district managers who rate the tool as 'useful' or 'very useful' in a post-adoption survey.
options.D: Total number of compliance summaries produced across the ninety-day window as a count of output volume.

items.question:
A department chair in the English department at a community college has developed an effective Claude workflow for drafting peer review feedback templates for faculty scholarship applications. The workflow took three iterations to optimise — the third version of the prompt produces consistently better outputs than the first. A colleague in the History department wants to adopt a similar workflow and asks for the materials.

What should the English chair share to give the History colleague the maximum benefit from her iteration experience?

options.A: The first version of the prompt so the History colleague can iterate through the same optimisation process and develop her own understanding of what works.
options.B: The final (third) version of the prompt along with a brief note explaining what was changed between each version and why, so the History colleague starts at the optimised version and understands the reasoning.
options.C: A narrative explanation of the English chair's experience using Claude without sharing the actual prompts, to avoid over-reliance on borrowed approaches.
options.D: All three versions of the prompt without explanation, so the History colleague can choose which version she finds most intuitive to work with.

items.question:
A research director at a commercial real estate firm is rolling out Claude to 10 research analysts who produce sector reports, client briefings, and market summaries. The analysts are highly skilled researchers but have no prior AI tool experience. She wants to ensure they can use Claude productively within their first two weeks of access.

Which TWO enablement investments would MOST efficiently achieve productive use within the two-week window? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A two-hour kickoff session featuring live demonstrations of Claude completing two real commercial real estate research tasks, with analysts observing and then immediately attempting the same tasks themselves.
options.B: A four-week self-directed learning programme covering advanced prompt engineering techniques, to be completed before analysts begin using Claude on any real research work.
options.C: A shared folder containing three pre-built prompt templates for the analysts' most common output types — sector reports, client briefings, and market summaries — each with step-by-step usage notes.
options.D: A structured first-week check-in session where each analyst shares one Claude-assisted draft with the research director and receives targeted feedback on prompt approach and output quality before proceeding to live client deliverables.
options.E: A pre-access briefing covering Claude's training methodology, knowledge cutoff dates, and model tier differences so analysts can make informed surface choices from day one.

items.question:
A compliance VP at a specialty pharmaceutical distributor has rolled out Claude to 22 compliance specialists for drafting deviation investigation reports. After four months, 16 specialists use it regularly. Six do not. When interviewed, five of the six state they are concerned that AI-drafted deviation reports might be perceived as less rigorous by the FDA during an inspection — that inspectors will question whether the compliance specialist actually performed the investigation.

What is the BEST response to this specific concern?

options.A: Verify the FDA's current guidance on AI-assisted documentation in deviation reports and incorporate the applicable requirements explicitly into the workflow documentation and prompt template.
options.B: Reassure the specialists verbally that the FDA has no policy against AI-assisted documentation, and encourage them to proceed with adoption.
options.C: Have the six specialists continue drafting deviation reports manually while the 16 adopters use Claude, creating a two-track quality comparison for the next inspection.
options.D: Redesign the workflow so Claude drafts only the background and evidence-gathering sections, while the specialist authors the investigation conclusion and corrective actions in their own words — and document the division of labour explicitly in the report.

items.question:
A programme director at an animal welfare charity needs a consistent Claude workflow for two types of communications: donor stewardship letters and volunteer recruitment messages. She has only one afternoon to set it up and wants it to be immediately usable by her two programme coordinators.

What is the MOST efficient setup that ensures both coordinators can produce consistent outputs immediately?

options.A: Write one master prompt that generates both a donor letter and a volunteer message in a single Claude session, saving time by combining both tasks.
options.B: Create two separate prompt templates — one for donor letters, one for volunteer messages — each specifying the audience, tone, required message elements, and one example of approved content, then share both with the coordinators.
options.C: Ask one coordinator to develop her own prompt for donor letters and the other to develop a prompt for volunteer messages, then compare results next week.
options.D: Set up a Claude Project with the charity's mission statement and programme descriptions uploaded as background knowledge, so coordinators can generate communications without specifying context each time.

items.question:
A planning manager at a port logistics operator introduced a Claude workflow nine months ago for drafting vessel-scheduling change notifications to freight customers. The notifications require accurate berth times, vessel names, and cargo cut-off deadlines. Over nine months, errors in AI-drafted notifications have led to three missed cargo cut-offs by freight customers. Each missed cut-off resulted in a customer claim. Operations staff spend more time correcting Claude drafts than they would drafting manually.

What is the MOST appropriate course of action?

options.A: Provide additional training to the operations staff on how to verify berth times and vessel details before submitting Claude-drafted notifications to customers.
options.B: Switch to a more capable model tier to reduce the frequency of factual errors in scheduling details before continuing the workflow.
options.C: Sunset the workflow: the task requires precision in time-sensitive operational data that Claude cannot reliably provide without structured data integration, and the current manual-drafting approach has better outcomes.
options.D: Narrow the workflow scope to notifications with no cargo cut-off implications, retaining Claude only for notifications that carry no financial risk if incorrect.

items.question:
A content strategy VP at a streaming media company is scaling a Claude-assisted content-briefing workflow from her five-person editorial team to all 40 content managers across three regional offices. The editorial team's workflow has been highly effective for six months and uses a refined prompt template and a shared Project with content standards.

Which TWO scaling elements are MOST critical to get right before the forty-person rollout begins? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Translate the editorial team's refined prompt template and Project instructions into written documentation that explains not just what the template says but why each element was designed that way, so regional managers can adapt it intelligently.
options.B: Appoint one champion in each regional office who has already reviewed the editorial team's workflow, received live coaching from a member of the editorial team, and can answer questions locally.
options.C: Conduct a satisfaction survey of the editorial team to collect a Net Promoter Score for the workflow before rolling it out, to use as baseline evidence of team endorsement.
options.D: Replace the Project custom instructions with a more detailed version that covers every possible content briefing scenario the regional offices might encounter.
options.E: Require the 40 content managers to complete a two-week prompt-engineering certification before accessing the shared Project.

items.question:
An asset management head at a transmission system operator has run a Claude programme for twelve months, using the tool to synthesise asset condition reports and maintenance prioritisation recommendations for 200 transmission assets. He presents the programme's metrics to the executive leadership team: Claude sessions run per month, analyst satisfaction scores, and reduction in synthesis time per asset. The operations director asks: 'Has any of this changed how we make maintenance decisions or reduced our unplanned outages?'

What does this question reveal about the programme's value evidence?

options.A: The operations director is applying an unreasonably short timeframe — twelve months is insufficient to observe statistically meaningful changes in unplanned outage rates for transmission infrastructure.
options.B: The operations director should be directed to the analyst satisfaction scores, which provide indirect evidence of improved decision-making quality through the analysts who make maintenance decisions.
options.C: The operations director is conflating operational reliability with AI programme contribution; unplanned outage rates depend on many variables beyond the quality of maintenance prioritisation.
options.D: The programme tracked tool adoption and efficiency gains but collected no evidence of whether synthesised recommendations were acted on, whether maintenance decision quality improved, or whether asset reliability outcomes changed — leaving the core operational value question unanswered.

items.question:
A change programme lead at a semiconductor manufacturer has just completed a successful two-month pilot of a Claude-assisted specification documentation workflow with eight process engineers. The pilot demonstrated strong quality and a 35% time reduction. She has approval to roll out to the full 60-person engineering team and has drafted a change management plan. Before launching, she realises her plan assumes all 60 engineers have the same level of AI familiarity as the eight pilot engineers — who self-selected because they were already interested in AI tools.

What should the change programme lead do NEXT?

options.A: Proceed with the rollout as planned; the 35% time reduction data will be compelling enough to overcome any familiarity gap during deployment.
options.B: Survey the 52 non-pilot engineers to assess their current AI familiarity level, prior tool experience, and specific concerns before finalising the change management and enablement plan.
options.C: Restrict the rollout to engineers who volunteer first, replicating the self-selection dynamic of the pilot until the majority choose to participate organically.
options.D: Revise the change management plan to include a tiered enablement track: a lighter track for engineers with prior AI tool experience and a more supported track for those without, then proceed with rollout.

items.question:
A grants manager at a cancer research hospital has used Claude for ten months to help draft grant applications. Over that period, the hospital submitted 18% more grant applications than the prior year and its success rate held steady at 32%. She is preparing a presentation to the hospital's development committee on the ROI of her AI programme.

How should she frame the ten-month results to make the strongest credible ROI case?

options.A: Focus on the 18% application volume increase alone, since the development committee primarily cares about output volume.
options.B: Present the success rate as the primary ROI metric because a stable 32% rate demonstrates that quality was not sacrificed for volume.
options.C: Calculate the financial value of the additional applications submitted at the historical success rate, and connect it to the programme's cost, to show expected grant revenue generated per dollar invested.
options.D: Avoid presenting any financial figures because grant award amounts vary widely and attributing specific revenue to Claude would overstate the programme's contribution.

items.question:
A knowledge management VP at a global management consulting firm is designing a firm-wide prompt library for 2,000 consultants across 15 practice areas. The library must be high-quality, kept current as client industry standards evolve, and used consistently rather than ignored. The VP has a programme management team of three people.

Which TWO governance mechanisms are MOST essential to sustaining the library's quality and adoption over a twelve-month horizon? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Assign a named prompt steward in each of the 15 practice areas who owns the quality and currency of that practice's templates, with a quarterly review cycle and a mechanism to propose updates.
options.B: Require all 2,000 consultants to submit every client deliverable prompt to the programme team for review before use, to maintain quality control.
options.C: Run a bi-annual firm-wide survey asking consultants how satisfied they are with the library to track engagement.
options.D: Embed the prompt library into the firm's existing knowledge management platform so consultants encounter it as part of their natural workflow rather than as a separate tool they must remember to visit.
options.E: Publish monthly usage analytics to practice area leads showing which templates are being used, which are being skipped, and which templates prompted the most subsequent editing — providing a usage signal for quality issues.

items.question:
An information management lead at a state environmental agency wants to run a first Claude pilot for her team of ten environmental permit analysts. The analysts review and respond to permit applications from industrial facilities. She has two candidate use cases: drafting acknowledgement letters to permit applicants, and drafting technical deficiency notices identifying missing information in incomplete applications.

Which is the BETTER first pilot use case for a public agency with no prior AI experience?

options.A: Acknowledgement letters, because they are low-stakes, formulaic in structure, and errors can be corrected before causing regulatory or stakeholder harm — giving the team a safe learning environment.
options.B: Technical deficiency notices, because the high complexity of the task will force analysts to engage deeply with the tool and develop stronger prompting skills more quickly.
options.C: Technical deficiency notices, because demonstrating Claude's capability on a complex regulatory task will make a stronger ROI case to the agency director.
options.D: Both simultaneously, because a public agency has an obligation to evaluate AI tools comprehensively before committing to any single use case.

items.question:
An L&D director at a telecom equipment vendor is designing Claude enablement for 30 technical trainers who deliver product training to enterprise customers. Trainers are expert communicators with deep product knowledge but varying comfort with AI. The L&D director's goal: every trainer can independently use Claude to customise standard training decks for specific customer contexts within two weeks of programme launch.

Which enablement design would MOST reliably achieve this specific goal?

options.A: Assign all 30 trainers a self-paced e-learning course covering Claude prompting theory and have them demonstrate completion before accessing any shared templates.
options.B: Provide each trainer with a ready-to-use prompt template for training deck customisation, run a ninety-minute hands-on session where each trainer customises one real deck for an upcoming customer, and designate two AI-confident trainers as on-call peers for the first two weeks.
options.C: Deploy a locked Claude interface pre-loaded with a customisation workflow, so trainers simply enter customer details and receive a customised deck without needing to learn prompting skills.
options.D: Require all 30 trainers to complete a four-hour live workshop covering Claude architecture, prompting best practices, and common failure modes before using the tool on any real content.

items.question:
A store operations VP at an independent grocery chain is rolling out a Claude workflow for drafting weekly store communication briefings to 35 store managers. After six weeks, 12 managers are active users and 23 have tried it once but reverted to drafting manually. Exit interviews reveal that the 23 managers felt the drafts were 'too generic' and 'didn't sound like they came from someone who knows our stores.'

What is the MOST direct cause of this reversion and how should the VP address it?

options.A: The 23 managers lack sufficient literacy to prompt Claude effectively, and a mandatory training programme should be run before the rollout continues.
options.B: The shared prompt template does not include fields for store-specific context — local events, team names, seasonal factors — so managers receive generic drafts that feel impersonal, and the template should be redesigned with required context fields.
options.C: Claude is fundamentally unsuited to drafting communication that requires store-level context, and the workflow should be narrowed to communications with no local customisation.
options.D: The managers' preference for manual drafting is driven by habit rather than quality, and more usage over time will naturally produce personalisation as they develop their own prompting habits.
